name: Orders

expected_models.name: Order
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped aggregate with customer snapshots, canonical state, totals, and audit metadata.

expected_models.name: OrderItem
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped item with optional product/variant reference and immutable commercial snapshots.

expected_features: Create and edit draft orders through services.
Confirm orders with immutable customer, product, and item snapshots.
Provide organization-scoped selectors, policies, HTML interfaces, audit, and outbox events.

states.requirement: Approved canonical state contract for Phase 03.
states.rule: Do not persist provider or legacy states as canonical states without an approved normalization contract.

snapshots: Confirmed orders retain customer name, optional normalized document, one primary operational contact, and existing default shipping and billing addresses.
Every item retains name, variant, SKU, unit, quantity, base price, discount, surcharge, gross total, and total snapshots.
Later Customer or Product changes never rewrite confirmed history.
Personal-data snapshots use a closed versioned schema, are masked for OPERATOR, and never enter audit, outbox, or logs.
Merged Customer or inactive/archived Product or ProductVariant blocks confirmation until explicit correction.
idempotency: All mutable commands use OrderCommandReceipt scoped by Organization, operation, and idempotency key.
The same key with a different canonical payload is an explicit conflict.
Outbox events use stable aggregate and event identifiers.
Retries never duplicate confirmation, history, or monetary effects.
Concurrent commands lock and revalidate the organization-scoped aggregate and expected_version.
Concurrent first-sequence creation is protected by a tenant constraint and PostgreSQL race handling.
money_rules: Use BRL and Decimal; never float.
Persist money as Decimal(14,2) and quantity as Decimal(12,3).
Round each line with ROUND_HALF_UP before aggregating persisted item values.
Server-side totals are authoritative and are recalculated from items.
Quantity, base price, discounts, surcharges, subtotal, and total satisfy database and service invariants.
Only manager-tier roles apply discounts or surcharges; every surcharge requires a reason and cannot represent shipping, tax, interest, or payment fees.
authorization: Organization comes from authenticated active Membership.
Every service and selector receives Organization explicitly.
Object identifiers are always resolved inside Organization.
Any active role may view, create and edit drafts, set base price, and confirm.
Only OWNER, ADMIN, and MANAGER may discount, surcharge, cancel, or view unmasked personal data.
Cross-organization reads and writes are refused and tested.

coverage.domain_expectation: Critical order rules require direct behavioral tests; aggregate coverage alone is insufficient.

documentation: ADRs for state, snapshots, idempotency, and money where needed
acceptance_criteria: The plan is explicitly approved before implementation.
Only allowed apps and features changed.
No later domain or external effect was introduced.
Organization isolation and authorization are enforced and tested.
Snapshots, states, money, idempotency, and concurrency follow approved contracts.
All quality gates and CI pass on the candidate HEAD.
Independent review has no unresolved blocker.
Human approval is explicit before PR, merge, state update, or next phase.

handoff_format.base_sha_semantics: The exact origin/main SHA resolved before branch creation; this is actual_base_sha in checkpoint reports.

allowed_scope: Planning and, only after plan approval, a new greenfield Orders domain.
Minimal approved adapters to existing Foundation, Customers, and Products contracts.
New Orders tests, migrations, documentation, audit, and outbox integration.
forbidden_scope: Starting Fulfillment, Payments, Messaging, Integrations, Dashboard, infrastructure, homologation, or cutover.
Changing approved Customers or Products rules without explicit human authorization.
Reusing Flowlog data, migrations, runtime, IDs, secrets, or infrastructure.
Deploying, configuring Coolify, merging, or starting the next phase.
